Collapse grant rows to distinct recipient identities

Source: R/dedup.R
pf_dedup_doc.Rd

The main scale lever for the full grant file. Grants repeat heavily — the same foundation funds the same charity every year, and thousands of foundations fund the same large charities — so matching distinct recipient identities rather than grant rows removes work without removing recall.

Details

It also buys recall outright. Because a cluster is one organization by construction, a match found for any member propagates to every member: a truncated, misspelled, or acronymic variant inherits the EIN resolved for an easier variant sitting in the same cluster. See pf_propagate_matches().

Two levels

"exact"

group by the normalized key (name_key, street_key, zip5). A hash group-by; linear and safe.

"fuzzy"

additionally cluster the surviving distinct keys — a much smaller set — within a geographic block, joining names whose Jaro-Winkler similarity clears threshold. Absorbs ST JUDES / ST JUDE CHILDRENS RESEARCH HOSP.

Guarding against over-merging

Two different organizations can share an address (FIRST PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH and FIRST PRESBYTERIAN FOUNDATION at one Boca Raton ZIP). Fuzzy clustering therefore requires high name similarity and applies npmatch's hard veto predicates — conflicting embedded numbers, ordinals, or directions — so LOCAL 32 never merges with LOCAL 45, nor FIRST with SECOND. Inspect the result with pf_dedup_report() before trusting it.
